title: DELTA: Robustly Training Label-Conditional Diffusion Models with Weak Annotations
claim: Naively trained conditional generators degrade under imperfect supervision, showing recurring, identifiable failure modes across different weak-label settings.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, class-labeled sample grids, color-coded failure boxes with legend below
description: Three side-by-side grids of generated ImageNette samples, one per weak-annotation setting: (a) noisy label, (b) ambiguous label, (c) semi-supervised data. Each grid has 10 rows, labeled on the far left with class names (Tench, English springer, Cassette player, Chain saw, Church, French horn, Garbage truck, Gas pump, Golf ball, Parachute), and 10 columns of small photo thumbnails. Colored rectangles are drawn over selected images or whole rows. Red marks class-image mismatch, green marks per-class homogenization, and yellow/orange marks low-quality generations. A legend with three colored boxes sits below the panels. Red boxes are scattered in (a). Wide yellow and green bands span entire rows in (b). Few, sparse boxes appear in (c). The eye goes first to the dense photo grids and the bright colored boxes.
caption: Randomly generated ImageNette samples from naive LCDMs trained under three forms of weak annotations: (a) noisy labels, (b) ambiguous labels, and (c) semi-supervised data. Colored boxes highlight three distinct failure modes that arise across these settings: class–image mismatch; per-class homogenization; and low-quality generations.
abstract: While label-conditional diffusion models have recently exhibited remarkable generative capabilities, their success heavily relies on massive, cleanly labeled datasets. In practice, categorical supervision is rarely perfect: it is often corrupted by noise, clouded by ambiguity, or partially missing. Training directly on such weak annotations severely degrades generation quality, and existing robust methods offer only fragmented solutions that depend on scarce auxiliary priors. To overcome these limitations, we propose DELTA, a unified framework that robustly trains Diffusion modELs across all three weak annoTAtion types. By treating the unknown true label as a latent variable, DELTA optimizes a principled variational objective that jointly recovers the clean data distribution and infers the true label posteriors. To make this joint training computationally tractable, we further introduce a median-centered timestep sampling strategy that efficiently concentrates estimation where the diffusion process is most informative. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DELTA produces high-fidelity, class-consistent samples across diverse weak supervision scenarios, outperforming specialized baselines while demanding strictly less prior knowledge.
